MikMarbleMod 3.23 — install
===========================

This bundle is a complete, ready-to-run UE4SS install with MikMarbleMod.

Requires the Season 73 version of Marbles on Stream (Steam build 26247165,
October 2026, or later). Older game builds need MikMarbleMod 3.21. See
"Important" at the bottom.

1. Find your game's Win64 folder:
   <Steam>\steamapps\common\Marbles on Stream\MarblesOnStream\Binaries\Win64\

2. Copy the CONTENTS of this zip into that Win64 folder:
     dwmapi.dll   -> lands next to MarblesOnStream-Win64-Shipping.exe
     ue4ss\       -> merges into the existing ue4ss\ folder (if you already have one)

3. Launch the game. UE4SS loads the mod from
     ue4ss\Mods\MikMarbleMod\dlls\main.dll

4. Confirm it worked. In ue4ss\UE4SS.log you should see:
     Using engine version: 5.8
     [MikMarble] Mod initialized (C++ v3.23) -> 127.0.0.1:5000/mod
     [MikMarble] target: default = 127.0.0.1:5000/mod (results on; events: none)


HTTP API
--------
Three endpoints, all POST, relative to each target's URL (for the default
target that is `path` from config.txt, default /mod). Out of the box only
/ready and /results are used, exactly as in 3.22; /event needs opting in
(see config.txt below).

1) POST {path}/ready — one-shot handshake once the mod is live.

   {"mod": "MikMarbleMod", "version": "3.23", "results": true, "events": []}

   Lets a backend know which build is talking to it and what this target will
   receive. Versions before 3.23 sent only mod + version, and before 3.21 an
   empty object {}, so treat every field as optional.

2) POST {path}/results — sent once per match, when the results are final.

   {
     "type": "race",
     "players": [
       {"name": "Alice", "finished": true,  "eliminations": 2},
       {"name": "Bob",   "finished": false, "eliminations": 0}
     ]
   }

   type          "race" (includes death race), "royale", or "bullseye"
   name          the player's display name
   finished      did they finish / survive
   eliminations  kills credited to that player (0 for environmental deaths,
                 and always 0 in bullseye)

   ORDER IS THE RESULT. Players are listed in placement order: winner FIRST,
   and the LAST entry is the loser. Finishers come first, then DNFs ordered so
   that the first player eliminated ends up last in the list.

   Notes per mode:
     race      finishers in finish order, then DNFs in reverse-elimination order
     royale    winner first, then everyone else in reverse-elimination order.
               If a royale TIMES OUT with marbles still alive, only the winner
               and the eliminated players are reported — the surviving
               mid-table players have no event-derived ranking.
     bullseye  ranked by distance to the target centre; every player reports
               finished: true. The game itself only scores the top three, so
               placements below the podium are a best-effort reconstruction —
               winner and loser are reliable, mid-field is approximate.

   The list can legitimately be EMPTY (e.g. every player is on the ignore list
   below), so handle that rather than assuming at least one entry.

3) POST {path}/event — live gameplay events (3.23+, only the ones you route).

   One flat JSON object per event. Every event has:
     event      the event name
     ts         Unix time in milliseconds
     match_id   the game's match GUID for this map (or null)
     map        map display name, e.g. "Battle Stadium"
     mode       "race", "royale", "bullseye", "laps", "tilted",
                "grand_prix_results" or "other"
   Player events also have "name" (same as in /results) and "display_name".

   map_entered          level, experience, grand_prix (bool)
   player_joined        command (the chat text, e.g. "!play 7", or null for
                        bots), via_chat (bool)
   countdown            phase ("start" = pre-race countdown, "race_end" =
                        force-race-end timer), seconds_left — once per second
   marble_damaged       damage (float), health (after the hit), health_before,
                        max_health, attacker (or null)
   marble_finished      position (1 = first), winner (bool)
   marble_eliminated    killer (or null for falls/zones), elimination_order
   marble_resurrected   (royale) an eliminated marble came back; detected_by
                        "respawn_hook" or "damage". A later death sends a
                        new marble_eliminated.
   grand_prix_finished  races, standings: [{position, name, display_name,
                        points, wins, eliminations, damage}, ...]

   Example:
   {"event": "player_joined", "ts": 1793980552202, "match_id": "7487a7ee-...",
    "map": "Marble Diner", "mode": "race", "name": "drdraxi",
    "display_name": "DrDraxi", "command": "!play 7", "via_chat": true}

   Events reach each target in the order they happened, and /results always
   arrives after that match's last finish/elimination event. A royale sends a
   lot of marble_damaged (hundreds per 30 marbles), so only route it where
   it's wanted.


config.txt
----------
On first launch the mod auto-creates:
     ue4ss\Mods\MikMarbleMod\config.txt

with these defaults (which match the bundled dummy server, server/server.py):

  host=127.0.0.1
  port=5000
  path=/mod        # target "default": POSTs to /mod/ready and /mod/results

  # Optional: players to leave out of reported results.
  # Comma-separated; the key may be repeated to add more.
  ignore=SomeName, AnotherName
  ignore=ThirdName

`ignore` is off by default. Matching is exact but CASE-INSENSITIVE, and is not
a partial match ("Bob" does not match "Bobby"). It applies to race, death race
and bullseye — but NOT to royale, where placement is derived from elimination
order and removing players would misreport who went out first and last.

On startup the mod prints the list it loaded, and after each match how many it
removed, so a typo is easy to spot:

  [MikMarble] ignore list: 2 name(s) loaded -> somename, anothername
  [MikMarble] ignore list: omitted 1 player(s) from results

Targets and live events (3.23+). Give each extra endpoint an id, then list
which ids get each feature. Live events are OFF unless listed:

  target.overlay=http://192.168.1.20:8080/marbles
  target.bot=https://example.com/hooks

  results=default                # the default when omitted; "none" = off
  player_joined=overlay,bot
  marble_eliminated=overlay
  countdown=overlay
  all_events=bot                 # shortcut: every live event to these ids

Feature keys: results, map_entered, player_joined, marble_finished,
marble_eliminated, marble_resurrected, marble_damaged, countdown,
grand_prix_finished, all_events.
The log shows the resolved routing at startup, plus a "[MikMarble] config:"
warning for an unknown id or a bad URL. `ignore` only affects /results, never
live events.

To use your own backend, edit config.txt after the first launch and restart.


Important — this bundle ships a custom UE4SS
--------------------------------------------
Marbles on Stream runs on Unreal Engine 5.8, which upstream UE4SS does not
support. This bundle therefore includes a patched build:

  ue4ss\UE4SS.dll
  ue4ss\UE4SS-settings.ini          (engine version set to 5.8)
  ue4ss\UE4SS_Signatures\FName_Constructor.lua
  ue4ss\UE4SS_Signatures\GUObjectArray.lua
  ue4ss\UE4SS_Signatures\GNatives.lua
  ue4ss\UE4SS_Signatures\GUObjectHashTables.lua

Do NOT replace these with a stock UE4SS release, and do not delete the
UE4SS_Signatures folder — without them UE4SS fails to start and no mod loads
at all (the log will show "PS scan timed out" after repeated "Scan failed",
"Engine version is not supported", or it will hang on "Waiting for object
construction...").

If you are upgrading from 3.21, copy the whole bundle again: the new files
are in ue4ss\UE4SS_Signatures\ and ue4ss\UE4SS-settings.ini, not only the DLL.
